title: Polynomial-Time Conjunction
statement: Let $p$ and $q$ be Boolean-valued functions on finite bit strings. If the functions sending $x$ to the one-bit outputs $[p(x)]$ and $[q(x)]$ are polynomial-time computable, then the function sending $x$ to $[p(x)\land q(x)]$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $p,q$ map finite bit strings to Boolean values
The one-bit output function $x\mapsto[p(x)]$ is polynomial-time computable
The one-bit output function $x\mapsto[q(x)]$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: Let $p$ and $q$ be Boolean-valued predicates on bit strings such that the maps sending $x$ to the one-bit words $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ are both polynomial-time computable (computed by some finite binary Turing machine within $C(n+1)^c$ steps on inputs of length $n$, for some constants $C, c$). Then the map sending $x$ to the one-bit word $p(x) \land q(x)$ is polynomial-time computable.
